Which stations run where in Dubai

Every counter on this page runs somewhere in Dubai, and the venue decides which ones. A private villa is the permissive case: outdoors on your own plot, the charcoal counter, the robata bed, the tandoor, the saj and the smoker all run. The line Dubai Municipality draws is enclosure — "do not light coal in an enclosed space or indoors" — and the UAE Fire Code keeps gas cylinders out of the house and off roofs and terraces (11-2.2.6, Table 11.1). Master-community rules treat the shared lawn, pool and beach differently from your own plot, so the fired counters sit on the plot and community security is told in advance.

Towers reverse it, and the rule is published: Emaar's vertical-community rules prohibit "barbecues, grills, or any cooking equipment of any kind" on balconies and terraces whatever the fuel, and no LPG cylinder may be brought into the tower or the unit. So in an apartment the tandoor, the smoker, the robata bed and the wood-fired oven stay out. The naan and the smoked brisket are fired in a licensed partner kitchen and finished on site, while an induction counter, an electric saj and a live carvery do the cooking your guests watch.

A yacht turns on one clause. No additional gas cylinder may be kept aboard (D-Marin Art. 53.1(a)), and Dubai Harbour bans the operation of gas cylinders and live fire on marina premises (section 7.4). That takes the tandoor, the saj dome and the shawarma spit off the boat menu. Charter crews run the vessel's own fitted grill for the mashawi and the skewers while the chef preps, plates and serves; induction, plancha and the carvery board come aboard unchanged.

On sand it depends which beach. Lighting a fire outside a designated zone on an open public beach is a Dubai Municipality offence carrying a Dh500 fine, and charcoal in the municipal beach parks is confined to the fixed BBQ stations, so an open beach is a carvery, raw-bar and induction menu. A permitted private event on beach land or a licensed beach club is a different case, and the fired counters come back with the permit stack behind them. For a rooftop or a desert site we put the setup to the building or the site operator and get it confirmed before quoting, because those two vary address by address.

Where a counter is refused the dish list does not shrink, the cooking moves. The smoker becomes a live carvery of the same brisket, since the theatre of smoking is the carve. Tandoor breads are baked in the licensed kitchen and finished on a tawa at the counter, with the tikka seared on a plancha. Robata keeps its counter and its skewers on an electric yakitori griddle. The saj goes electric. Charcoal becomes gas or electric, and the menu above stays as written.
Dietary variants, stated honestly

Halal is the default across this category in Dubai and is table stakes, not a selling point. Vegetarian food gets its own counter, set out as named dishes, not as a promise. Vegan and plant-based grilling is available and worth flagging at the brief, because the marinades change. Gluten-free is the weakest link in this market: most Dubai grill menus name it as an accommodation without saying which dishes qualify, so ask and the menu comes back marked dish by dish. Pork does not appear. If you brief by ratio, as many hosts do, give us the vegetarian to non-vegetarian split and the counters are built to it.
What this page is not

Two searches land here that we cannot answer, and it is fairer to say so than to let you read on. Live cooking classes are a teaching product, where a chef runs a session and you do the cooking; this is the reverse, and the chef at the counter does the cooking while you stay a guest. Searches for live music restaurants in Dubai arrive here too, and we are not a restaurant and do not book entertainment. What does carry across from live cooking station restaurants is the counter itself: an open pass, a chef in full view, and the plate handed over the moment it is finished.
